text:
Amanda (People Ops): quick Q — new hire Jake (AU passport) is on/renewing an E-3 and asked about timing for stamping, whether we can reimburse courier fees, and if he can start remotely from AU while waiting for an appointment. tagging @Marco for legal. start date currently tentatively 2026-05-04.

Ben (PM): flexible on start — fine with remote for a few weeks if needed.

Jake Smith: hey all — correct, I'm in Sydney. current E-3 stamp expires 2026-06-10. I can either renew at the consulate here or try to do any extension from the US if needed. My main Qs: 1) do you need my passport at any point? 2) can I start remote before stamping? 3) how does payroll/benefits work if I'm remote from AU for a few weeks?

Tara (People Ops): short answers: we do NOT keep employee passports. we reimburse courier fees for consulate stamping (you must keep receipts). Section 1 of I-9 can be completed remotely; Section 2 must be done in person once you're physically in the US for your start date (or at an approved third party per policy). we'll confirm details with counsel re: I-9 timing.

Marco (Immigration Counsel): quick clarifying points (non-legal advice summary): E-3 workflow: employer obtains LCA (DOL) — employer provides a copy to the candidate. For consular renewals the candidate applies at a US consulate with: LCA copy, offer letter, degree documents, passport, DS-160 confirmation and photo. Employer does NOT retain passport. For renewals: consulate route is common; USCIS I-129 filing inside the US is possible but slower/less common for routine renewals. Employer can reimburse visa-related expenses. I-9: employer must complete Section 2 within 3 business days after an employee's US start date. If employee's first work days are remote outside US, Section 2 is completed after arrival to US. I'll send a short packet checklist to you and Jake.

Jake Smith: practical follow-ups — 1) which courier/address should I use? 2) what exactly should I include in the consulate packet? 3) will payroll start while I'm in AU or only after I'm on US payroll?

Tara (People Ops): answers: 1) you will book via the consulate's portal (Sydney consulate uses VFS/consulate courier) — we do not ship on your behalf, but we will reimburse approved courier fees once you submit receipts. 2) typical packet: passport, LCA, signed offer letter (PDF we will DM to you), original degree or certified copy, DS-160 confirmation, passport photo, any past pay stubs (if asked). Marco will share a checklist. 3) payroll: Redwood currently runs US payroll only. if you want to be paid while resident in AU we can explore a short contractor engagement (Finance approval required). otherwise US payroll will begin when you're onboarded onto US payroll (i.e., after you have valid US work authorization and have completed onboarding steps). tagging @Ben to confirm manager flexibility.

Ben (PM): we can do a 2-4 week contractor arrangement so Jake can start contributing immediately. preference remains to shift to US payroll once he's physically in the US.

Marco (Immigration Counsel): checklist I'll provide: - LCA (signed copy) - Signed offer letter - DS-160 confirmation page - Passport (valid 6+ months) - 1 passport photo - Original degree or certified copy - Proof of professional qualifications/experience - Evidence of ties/home country (if consulate asks) Note: processing times vary by consulate; book early. If you want, counsel can review materials before you go to appointment.

Amanda (People Ops): action items: - Amanda to DM Jake LCA + offer PDF (owner: Amanda) - Tara to draft short contractor agreement for interim pay (owner: Tara) - Finance to confirm contractor pay cadence & approval for AU contractor (owner: Finance; Tara to loop) - Marco to send E-3 packet checklist and quick review offer (owner: Marco) - Jake to book consulate appointment and paste tracking number here for reimbursement (owner: Jake) Tentative start date held at 2026-05-04 but flexible.

Jake Smith: thanks — booking appointment today. will share confirmation + tracking once courier booked.

visa-bot: Reminder: upload courier/visa receipts to `/expenses` within 30 days and tag "Visa-courier" for reimbursement processing.

Tara (People Ops): one more thing on benefits: benefits eligibility kicks in only once on US payroll. we'll provide a benefits snapshot showing effective date once payroll status is confirmed.

Ben (PM): fine by me — thanks everyone.

---
Sample reimbursement email (paste into `/expenses` submission):

```
Subject: Visa courier - Jake Smith - E-3 stamping
Body: Hi Finance — attached receipt and tracking for courier used to submit passport to Sydney consulate. Amount: $XX. Date: YYYY-MM-DD. Please reimburse to Jake via payroll/expense system.
Attachments: courier receipt (pdf), consulate tracking (screenshot)
```

If anyone needs the LCA/offer PDFs or a one-pager checklist, I have them ready to DM.

Amanda (People Ops): will DM now. Jake — ping here when you have the tracking number and we'll process reimbursement. :thumbsup:
